My company recently signed a VERY large Splunk contract (I can't say how much, as it might identify us in some way). We used Logstash and looked at a few other options as well. In fact, one company we looked at had a sales team so bad that they complained that they weren't given a chance during the sale process (can't name them either, but it should be obvious if you ever talk to them). Needless to say, that company lost LOTS of business due to their sales antics and missed out on a sale because their product was 1/3 of what Splunk is. (Note: If you're a company that does sales calls via computer - ie: Skype, Bluejeens, Go2Meeting, etc, make sure your damn Webcam is off before you're on the call, or at least cover it with tape...)

We basically found Logstash slowed down a lot if you didn't have a **full time** admin giving it attention, helping people with their queries or dancing like a drunken sailor half the week. We also found that the user community was a little clunky compared to Splunk - well, a lot clunky. After 2 failed Logstash attempts, we decided we were done. Some of the business still uses Logstash, but the huge majority is migrating over and we'll probably spend about 3 minutes convincing the rest to drop Logstash.

Don't get me wrong, FOSS is fine in certain situations, but when you have hard requirements for reporting (industry, not just "policy"), using OSS can be a complete PITA, not to mention hardware requirements and crap. In my experience, FOSS is fine for smaller and mid-sized environments, but when you go large or super-large, things change drastically.
